sections.h2: What is the fastest way to sell a house in Dunwoody, GA?
sections.html:
The fastest route is usually an as-is cash sale, where the buyer takes the house in its current condition and closes on a date you choose. Listing with an agent and selling on your own are the other two options, and both can bring a higher price when the house is in good shape.

Dunwoody is the largest of the four cities in this set of Georgia pages. The Census Bureau estimates 51,792 residents as of July 1, 2025, only 0.3% above the April 2020 base of 51,643, so growth has been flat while the city was already built out. With little vacant land, most sales here are resales of existing homes, and a house with deferred repairs competes against updated ones in the same price range.

An as-is sale fits owners who inherited a house, are relocating, hold a house with tenants, or want to skip the cost and delay of repairs before a listing.

sections.h2: What do the Census numbers show about Dunwoody housing?
sections.html:
Dunwoody is a higher-income, higher-value city. The median value of owner-occupied homes is $602,900 for 2020 to 2024, median household income is $121,903, and 72.2% of adults 25 and older hold at least a bachelor's degree. Median gross rent is $1,859. About 56.2% of homes are owner-occupied and 89.1% of residents lived in the same house a year earlier, so most households stay put.

The city covers 13.03 square miles of land with 3,967.7 people per square mile (2020). Median selected monthly owner costs run $2,675 with a mortgage and $955 without. Commutes are short, at a mean of 24.9 minutes.

sections.h2: Can I rent out a Dunwoody house by the night, and does that change what it sells for?
sections.html:
No. The City of Dunwoody's Code of Ordinances forbids short-term rentals of single-family and multi-family residences, including rentals of less than 30 days through services such as Vrbo, Airbnb and HomeToGo. Enforcement is complaint-driven.

The code also bans party houses, meaning homes used for a commercial party that guests pay to attend. Only special event facilities can host those, and they need special event permits. The rule does not cover personal social gatherings. The city asks residents to call 911 for noise and traffic complaints, since most problems occur on weekends and after business hours.

For a seller, this takes a nightly-rental buyer out of the pool. Buyers who want income from the property are left with long-term leases, so a Dunwoody house with a tenant on a standard lease is marketed on that basis. If you have been renting by the night, stop before listing and do not describe that use in your marketing.

sections.h2: Which schools and amenities do Dunwoody buyers ask about?
sections.html:
Dunwoody students attend the DeKalb County School District, and the city's own schools page sends visitors to the district site. The district's home page describes itself as the third largest in Georgia, with more than 90,300 students and 137 schools and centers. School assignment depends on the address, so use the district's tools for your exact street instead of quoting a school name from memory.

Buyers also ask about parks and public spaces. The city's site highlights Dunwoody Village, Brook Run Park, a public art exhibit at the Dunwoody Nature Center at Dunwoody Park, and a Veterans Day ceremony. A local nonprofit, the Dunwoody Preservation Trust, runs the historic Donaldson-Bannister Farm as an event venue.

The Census adds context on who lives here: 24.6% of residents are under 18 and 13.5% are 65 or older, so both families and older owners are part of the market.

sections.h2: How are Dunwoody property taxes billed and paid?
sections.html:
Dunwoody sits in DeKalb County, so the DeKalb County Tax Commissioner bills and collects the property tax. Bills are mailed to the owner of record as of January 1 and also to the current owner when that is someone different. The county adds that not receiving a bill does not remove the duty to pay.

The county takes current-year payments from August 15 through November 15 and allows two installments. The first has to be paid before the second, and anything unpaid after a due date draws penalties or interest. Partial payments are allowed. A payment counts as on time only if the county receives it by the due date, and for mailed checks the county goes by the USPS postmark.

Online payment by e-check carries no transaction fee, while card payments carry a percentage fee set by the county. Prior-year balances are mailed to a separate delinquent collections division.

sections.h2: What should I gather before I sell a Dunwoody house?
sections.html:
Collect the documents a buyer and title company will request, then check city and county records for anything that could slow the closing:

  • The deed, and any trust or estate papers that show who may sign.
  • Loan payoff statements for every mortgage or lien.
  • The DeKalb tax account showing current installments and any delinquent amount.
  • Permit records from the city's Community Development department, including any open work.
  • Any rental or lease agreements, since Dunwoody does not allow stays under 30 days.

The city offers an online portal for licenses and permits, and its code of ordinances is searchable on the website. If the house has an unpermitted addition or an open code complaint, find that out before the buyer's inspector does.

sections.h2: How does a cash offer on a Dunwoody home compare with listing it?
sections.html:
A cash offer gives you speed and fewer moving parts, and a listing gives you the chance at a higher price. In a city where homes are valued well above the national picture, the gap between the two can be large, so ask for the numbers instead of assuming.

Request written terms from each buyer. Ask who pays closing costs, how many days to close, whether the offer depends on an inspection or financing, and what happens if the buyer walks away. Then work out what you would net after the mortgage payoff, tax bills and liens, using figures from your lender and the closing attorney.

Owners who are relocating, settling an estate, or facing a hard deadline tend to value certainty, while owners with a move-in-ready house and a flexible timeline usually do better on the open market.

sections.h2: Are there local business and zoning rules that matter if I run a business from my house?
sections.html:
Possibly. Dunwoody requires a business license for any business that has a physical location in the city, and the city runs a portal for licenses and permits. Home-based businesses should confirm their status with the licensing office before a sale, because a buyer will want to know whether any certificate transfers or ends.

The city's Planning Commission and its list of planning, zoning and variance decisions show what is being considered near the Perimeter Center area and elsewhere. Look at those pages if a rezoning or redevelopment is happening near your street, since buyers sometimes ask about it.

Disclose what you know. Information shared early keeps a cash sale or a listing from falling apart during the title and inspection period.

faqs.q: Are Airbnb rentals allowed in Dunwoody?
faqs.a: No. The city code forbids short-term rentals of single-family and multi-family homes, including stays under 30 days booked through Vrbo, Airbnb and similar services. Enforcement is complaint-driven.

faqs.q: Who collects property tax on a Dunwoody house?
faqs.a: The DeKalb County Tax Commissioner. Current-year payments run from August 15 through November 15, with two installments allowed and penalties on late amounts.

faqs.q: What is the median home value in Dunwoody?
faqs.a: The Census Bureau lists $602,900 as the median value of owner-occupied homes in Dunwoody for 2020 to 2024. That is a citywide survey figure, not a price for any one house.
The DeKalb County School District. The city's schools page points to the district, and your street address decides which schools your home is assigned to.

faqs.q: Can I sell a Dunwoody house with a tenant in it?
faqs.a: Yes. Give the buyer a copy of the lease and the deposit details. A buyer who plans to keep the tenant needs to know the lease terms, and one who wants the house empty will price that in.
